Fit a Fixed-Range Spatial Abundance Field to a Distance-Removal Model

Source: R/gdr_response_field_fit.R
fit_gdr_response_field.Rd

Replace the independent random intercepts on abundance in a native TMB distance-removal (GDR) model with a spatially correlated Gaussian field. Nearby survey blocks then tend to have similar density deviations. The correlation between two blocks falls with the distance d between them as exp(-d / range). You supply range; it is not estimated. Ecological scales of effect remain separate parameters, estimated later with make_gdr_refitter() and multiScale_optim().

Usage

fit_gdr_response_field(
  model,
  coords,
  crs,
  range,
  cold_starts,
  audit_dir,
  tmb_settings,
  max_memory_mb = 512
)

Arguments

model

An unmarkedFitGDR fitted by unmarked::gdistremoval() with engine = "TMB". It serves as the template. Its data, formulas, cutoff K and estimates are reused, and its independent abundance intercepts become the field. See "Check that your model qualifies" for the supported model forms.

coords

Numeric matrix or data frame with two projected coordinate columns (x, y) and one row per survey, in the row order of the model's frame. Row names must equal the frame's site row names, which are rownames(unmarked::siteCovs(model@data)) when the frame has site covariates. All surveys in one block (one level of the abundance grouping factor) must carry exactly the same coordinates, usually the block center, and different blocks must have different coordinates.

crs

The projected coordinate reference system of coords, as an EPSG code (for example 32617) or any other input accepted by sf::st_crs(). It must have two horizontal axes and declared linear units. Coordinates are never transformed, so range and coords must use these units.

range

Positive number. The fixed correlation range of the exponential field, in the linear units of crs. Two blocks range apart have correlation exp(-1), about 0.37, and blocks three ranges apart have correlation about 0.05. This is a distance over which density deviations are shared. It is not a kernel scale of effect, and it is not counted as a parameter.

cold_starts

Named list of one or more extra starting vectors (for example list(cold = cold)). Each vector holds one value for every fixed coefficient and log standard deviation, on the link scales listed by gdr_start_values(). Supply it either unnamed, in the order of gdr_start_values(model)$starts, or named by parameter block and position, such as "beta_lambda[1]" (log density intercept), "beta_dist[1]" (log distance scale), "beta_rem[1]" (logit removal probability) and "lsigma_lambda[1]" (log SD of the abundance intercepts). Each vector must differ from the template's estimates and from the other vectors. The names "original" and "final" are reserved.

audit_dir

Character string naming a directory for audit records. It is created if needed. Every fit writes small .rds records there: the request, the validated inputs, each attempt (including failures), the optimizer result saved before covariance work, and the final outcome. Records hold numbers, settings and identities, not fitted models. Keep the directory to inspect a failed fit.

tmb_settings

Named list of optimizer settings with elements method, se, threads and control. This function requires method = "BFGS", se = TRUE, threads = 1 and a positive integer control$maxit, for example list(method = "BFGS", se = TRUE, threads = 1L, control = list(maxit = 2500L, reltol = 1e-10)). The optional elements random.start, inner.control and record_memory are described in make_gdr_refitter(). Pass the identical list to make_gdr_refitter() when you later estimate scales of effect with the field.

max_memory_mb

Positive number, default 512. A conservative planning budget, in MiB, for the dense field covariance and the TMB tape. The fit stops before optimizing when its estimate exceeds the budget. The same budget limits later predict() calls on the fitted object. It is an estimate, not an operating-system memory cap.

Value

An object of class unmarkedFitGDRField. It extends the unmarkedFitGDR class of unmarked, so coef(), logLik(), unmarked::sigma() and summary() work as usual, while predict(), vcov() and confint() use the retained field covariance. The table under "Read the fitted model" says where each parameter lives and on what scale. The log-likelihood is the native Laplace approximation of the marginal likelihood, with the field integrated out. The AIC counts the same parameters as the template model, because the range is fixed. The attribute msr_gdr_refit_audit summarizes the fit: status, the attempts from every start with their diagnostics, the index of the selected start, maximum_start_value_difference (the spread of the negative log-likelihoods among starts) and the audit path.

Details

A random intercept for each survey block lets density differ among blocks beyond what the covariates explain. In the template model those block deviations are independent. This function keeps the same distance and removal observation model, the same cutoff K and the same SD of the deviations, but makes the deviations of nearby blocks correlated. See the "Model spatial correlation among survey blocks" section of vignette("v12-distance-removal", package = "multiScaleR") for a worked example.

Check that your model qualifies

The template must have all of the following:

  • Poisson abundance (mixture = "P") and a half-normal distance function (keyfun = "halfnorm").

  • Density output in birds per square kilometer (output = "density", unitsOut = "kmsq").

  • One visit per point (one primary period) and complete counts for every survey, with no sites dropped by unmarked.

  • Distance bands in meters with boundaries c(0, 25, 75) or c(0, 25, 50, 75), so the survey circle has a 75 m radius.

  • Exactly one random intercept in the abundance formula, such as ~ land1 + (1 | block). Every level of the grouping factor must have at least one survey.

  • Optionally, one independent random intercept in the distance formula, such as an observer effect. It stays independent. The removal formula takes no random effects.

  • No offset() terms.

  • unmarked 1.5.2 and TMB 1.9.25.

The field correlation matrix must also be numerically positive definite. Blocks at nearly identical locations relative to range can fail this check. No numerical jitter is added.

How the fit is checked

The field model is fitted from the template's own estimates (the start named "original") and from every vector in cold_starts. Each fit starts its block deviations at zero. Every start must return a converged, warning-free fit with usable covariance and a largest absolute gradient below 0.001. All starts must also agree, with negative log-likelihoods within 1e-5 and coefficients and log SDs within 0.001 of one another. If any start fails or the starts disagree, the function stops with an error and leaves the records in audit_dir. When every check passes, it returns the fit with the highest likelihood. Agreement among a few starts does not prove that no better optimum exists. If the starts disagree, compare the attempts recorded in audit_dir before trying other starting values.

Read the fitted model

QuantityWhere to find itScaleHow to read it
Density interceptcoef(fit)["lambda(Int)"]logexp() gives density per square km when covariates and the field are zero
Abundance covariate effectcoef(fit)["lambda(x)"]logexp() is the factor by which density changes per unit of x
Distance scalecoef(fit)["dist(Int)"]logexp() gives the half-normal scale in meters
Removal probabilitycoef(fit)["rem(Int)"]logitplogis() gives the probability, per unit of interval time, that a bird present is first detected
Field SDunmarked::sigma(fit)log densityTypical size of a block deviation. A block one SD above zero has exp(SD) times the density of a block with no deviation
Block deviationscoef(fit, type = "lambda", fixedOnly = FALSE)log densityThe entries labeled lambda(b_lambda), one fitted field value per block, follow the fixed coefficients
Correlation rangefit@response_field$definition$rangeCRS unitsSupplied by you, not estimated

Internally, TMB works with uncorrelated (whitened) versions of the block deviations. Every value reported by coef(), vcov() and predict() is converted back to the physical field, the deviation at each block's location.

How uncertainty is reported

vcov() returns the covariance retained from the fit. It includes the covariance between components (abundance, distance, removal) and between the fixed coefficients and the field values. It is computed once during fitting, so vcov() does not rerun TMB.

predict() uses that covariance for its standard errors. At a block used in fitting, the SE comes from the fitted coefficients and field values alone. At a new location, the SE adds the field variance that remains after conditioning on the fitted blocks. That extra variance describes how uncertain the field is between blocks. It is not observation noise. Density predictions are exp() of the linear predictor at the fitted field values. They are not averages over possible field values, which would be larger. With re.form = NA, predictions set the field to zero, which describes a block with no deviation rather than an average over blocks.

All of these intervals treat the ecological scales of effect and the correlation range as known. They add no uncertainty for either.

Estimate scales of effect with the field in place

Build a refit function from the field fit, using the same starts and the identical tmb_settings, and pass it to multiScale_optim():

refit <- make_gdr_refitter(field_fit, list(cold = cold),
  audit_dir = tempfile("gdr-field-refits-"), tmb_settings = settings)
opt <- multiScale_optim(field_fit, kernel_inputs, refit_fn = refit,
  n_cores = 1)

Each candidate scale refits the field from every start, with the range held fixed. Expect minutes even for 100 surveys. The search must run on one core with the default backend = "refit" and PSOCK = FALSE. The ordinary update() method stops for this class. Use the refit function instead.

Map density with the field

A density map needs the field value at every raster cell. Bind the fitting coordinates to the scale-of-effect result with response_field_geometry(), then pass the descriptor to predict.multiScaleR():

geometry <- response_field_geometry(opt, coords = block_xy, crs = 32617)
layers <- kernel_scale.raster(land, multiScaleR = opt,
  scale_center = TRUE, match_buffer = TRUE)
dens <- predict(opt, layers, type = "lambda", se.fit = TRUE,
  uncertainty = "conditional",
  raster_args = list(field_geometry = geometry))

The raster CRS must match crs, and prediction runs on one core. Each cell gets the field value predicted at its center from the fitted block values. The grouping factor of the field (block above) is not needed as a raster. A factor that also enters a fixed part of the model still needs an explicit value through site_values in kernel_scale.raster() or a raster coded with the fitted levels. To map the zero-field reference instead, omit field_geometry and set re.form = NA.

Not supported

Estimating the range, other abundance mixtures or distance functions, repeat visits with availability, a removal field, simulate(), profile(), ranef() and spatial cross-validation are not available for this model.

See also

unmarkedFitGDRField, make_gdr_refitter(), gdr_start_values(), response_field_geometry(), vignette("v12-distance-removal", package = "multiScaleR")

Examples

# \donttest{
# The field needs unmarked 1.5.2 and TMB 1.9.25.
if (requireNamespace("TMB", quietly = TRUE) &&
    utils::packageVersion("unmarked") == "1.5.2" &&
    utils::packageVersion("TMB") == "1.9.25") {
  # Eight survey blocks 1 km apart along a line, six point counts in each
  block <- factor(rep(paste0("b", 1:8), each = 6))
  hab <- rep(seq(-1, 1, length.out = 6), 8)
  shift <- c(-0.4, -0.3, -0.1, 0, 0.1, 0.2, 0.35, 0.4)[block]
  sim <- sim_dat_gdr(density = exp(log(400) + 0.5 * hab + shift),
    distance_scale = 40, removal = 0.2, dist_breaks = c(0, 25, 50, 75),
    interval_lengths = c(2, 3, 5), interval_units = "minutes",
    site_covs = data.frame(hab = hab, block = block), seed = 1)
  umf <- sim$observed

  # Template: an independent random intercept for each block (TMB engine)
  template <- unmarked::gdistremoval(lambdaformula = ~ hab + (1 | block),
    removalformula = ~ 1, distanceformula = ~ 1, data = umf,
    keyfun = "halfnorm", mixture = "P", output = "density",
    unitsOut = "kmsq", K = 60, engine = "TMB",
    starts = c(log(400), 0, log(40), qlogis(0.2), log(0.3)))

  # Every survey carries the projected coordinates (m) of its block center
  block_xy <- cbind(x = 500000 + 1000 * (as.integer(block) - 1),
                    y = 4400000)
  rownames(block_xy) <- rownames(unmarked::siteCovs(umf))

  # A second set of starting values, named by parameter block and position
  cold <- c("beta_lambda[1]" = log(300), "beta_lambda[2]" = 0,
            "beta_dist[1]" = log(30), "beta_rem[1]" = qlogis(0.4),
            "lsigma_lambda[1]" = log(0.5))
  settings <- list(method = "BFGS", se = TRUE, threads = 1L,
                   control = list(maxit = 2500L, reltol = 1e-10))

  field_fit <- fit_gdr_response_field(template, coords = block_xy,
    crs = 32617, range = 2000, cold_starts = list(cold = cold),
    audit_dir = tempfile("gdr-field-"), tmb_settings = settings)

  # Log density, log distance scale (m) and logit removal probability
  print(unmarked::coef(field_fit))
  # SD of the block deviations, on the log density scale
  print(unmarked::sigma(field_fit))
  # The range adds no parameter, so the AIC penalty matches the template
  print(c(template = template@AIC, field = field_fit@AIC))
}
#> lambda(Int) lambda(hab)   dist(Int)    rem(Int) 
#>   6.1293802   0.4423489   3.6600799  -1.6307798 
#>    Model Groups        Name     sigma      lower   upper
#> 1 lambda  block (Intercept) 0.2465782 0.09603057 0.63314
#> template    field 
#> 581.9212 580.3834 
# }
